task_description:
Analyze and fix a SonarQube warning in a project without introducing a new warning
- analyzer: SonarQube, server inside the instance, fed by its scanner
- SonarQube's report is the verdict
candidate_definition: ONE INSTANCE = one SonarQube warning identified by (rule key, file, line, project, revision), harvested from one repository commit (head_sha) whose message says a warning was fixed and names the rule, where the violating revision is the commit's parent (or a nearby earlier revision) and the fixed revision is head_sha (or a few commits on); the two revisions need not be parent and child. One commit may clear several warnings; the builder records that and keeps exactly one as the instance's target. The diff between the two revisions is kept verbatim as the reference answer and may carry unrelated edits.
source_requirements:
- from their history: a revision with the warning, and a later one where it is gone (the next
  commit or a few commits on); they need not be parent and child
- the developer's change: the diff between those two revisions, kept as a reference answer;
  it may carry unrelated edits
- rules: any SonarQube Java rule; no list, no exclusions
- one commit may clear several warnings; the builder records that and keeps one as the
  instance's target
- prefer projects that seem to fix sonarqube warnings
- a candidate is a repository at one commit whose message says a warning was fixed and names
  the rule; that commit is head_sha
- before recording a candidate the search checks three things with git alone, no analyzer and
  no build:
    the commit has a parent
    its diff modifies an existing .java file, not only adds new ones
    the message or the diff names sonar, squid, or a rule id like java:S1234
  a candidate that fails any of the three is not recorded
- what the search hands the builder, and the only two fields it records, spelled exactly so:
    clone_url  the repository's clone URL
    head_sha   the commit it found
  every other field of an instance is the builder's to establish; do not rename these two
criteria: Both the violating and the fixed revision compile offline inside the instance image with the recorded build command and the pre-fetched dependency cache. The shipped check.sh exits nonzero at the violating revision and zero at the fixed revision, verified by the builder with the observed exit codes recorded. The recorded warning (rule key, file, line) appears in the SonarQube issue list at the violating revision and is absent from the issue list at the fixed revision, both lists shipped with the instance. Applying the reference patch (the developer's diff between the two revisions) to the violating revision makes check.sh pass; applying an empty patch leaves it failing. Reverting the developer's change inside the fixed revision makes check.sh fail again (negative control executed by the builder). The instance records the exact SonarQube version, scanner version, active rule set/quality profile, and the exact compile and analyze commands used, and the check re-uses exactly those. The enclosing method or class declaration containing the warning is recorded verbatim so criterion (2) of the oracle is decidable. The instance analyzes only against the in-instance SonarQube server; no network access occurs during checking. The builder's own verification record ships with the instance, including the numbers it observed (issue counts at both revisions, exit codes of every demonstration run).

quality_gates_list: reproducibility: re-verify a sample of instances across 3 clean-environment reruns, requiring identical check verdicts
corruption sensitivity: a deliberately corrupted instance (negative control — developer's change reverted in the fixed revision) must be rejected by the pipeline's own gates
deduplication: near-duplicate instances removed (same repository + same rule + overlapping file, and identical reference diffs)
the shipped scripts run on a fresh Docker-only machine without crashing
rule spread enforced: no more than 15 shipped instances carry the same rule key
instance_format: a directory of scripts under /bench: Dockerfile, setup.sh, instance.json, checkout.sh, compile.sh, apply_patch.sh, check.sh, revert_fix.sh; instance.json carries clone_url, head_sha, violating_sha, fixed_sha, rule_key, rule_severity, warning_file, warning_line, enclosing_declaration, project_key, build_tool, build_command, scan_command, sonarqube_version, scanner_version

examples.description: A Maven Java repo (>=1000 stars, not a fork, pushed within 6 months) has commit abc123 'Fix sonar java:S2259 possible NPE in Parser.java'. It has a parent, its diff modifies the existing src/main/java/.../Parser.java, and the message names java:S2259. The builder analyzes parent and head with SonarQube 25.5.0.107428: java:S2259 at Parser.java:412 is present at the parent and absent at head. Instance target = that warning.
A commit whose message mentions sonar but which only ADDS new .java files and modifies none — refused at the corroboration gate before any clone-build cost is paid.
